newsitem.title: USA: Analysts peg U.S cotton crop 13.70-14.3 mln acres.
newsitem.headline: Analysts peg U.S cotton crop 13.70-14.3 mln acres.

text.p: Market analysts expect the U.S. Department of Agriculture to peg planted cotton area anywhere from 13.7 million to 14.3 million acres in its first official estimate of the new crop.
The USDA will issue its report March 31 at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.

Some industry sources said high prices for soybeans and corn could lure growers away from cotton, while others said rain in the Delta and the Southeast could delay corn plantings, thereby shifting land to cotton.

"The tradeoffs may be a wash," Carl Anderson, a cotton marketing specialist with Texas A & M University, said. Nonetheless, he pegged the USDA's estimate for the 1997/98 cotton crop at the low end of the range at 13.7 million acres.
Last year, U.S. cotton growers planted 14.67 million acres.
Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said fluctuating prices for corn and soybeans coupled with rain in the Delta, could ultimately alter her estimate of 13.93 million acres.
"Actual cotton area could be 300,000 acres above or below our estimate," she said.
Other analysts said talk of lower cotton acreage has been exaggerated.

David Brandon, a Memphis-based cotton analyst with Smith Barney, pegged the forecast at 14.2 million acres. He said the Southeast and the Delta will benefit from recent rains, which have caused delays in corn plantings.
"We will have some acres moving from corn to cotton," O.A. Cleveland, a cotton marketing specialist with Mississippi State University said, pegging the estimate at 13.9 million acres.

Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes put the forecast at 14.065 million acres. She said that while cotton prices remain comparatively low, the costs associated with growing cotton, including equipment, will prevent some farmers from switching to other crops.
Jarral Neeper of Calcot Ltd agreed. "There is a lot of money invested in the cotton industry," he said, pegging the crop at 14.25 million acres.
"I'm not convinced growers will abandon cotton."
Ryan Powell, a cotton analyst with Allendale, put the estimate at the top of the range at 14.3 million acres.
The greatest losses in cotton area are expected to show up in the Southeast, the Delta, and the West.
The USDA's estimate is based on conditions during the last week of April and the first week in March. The next planted area estimate will be released in June.
